title: Annotatio V §.XII (4): Luther charge — hostile letter / Marburg Oral-denial as faith-assault
pass_a_gloss: (4.) Of LUTHER, whose Testimony he marvels I alleged, namely drawn from an Epistle hostile to the Reformed — especially since it is moreover known that Luther at Marburg, where the Holy Supper was chiefly disputed between Luther and Zwingli, so judged Zwinglian errors, and among them the denial of Oral Eating, deadly and assaulting the foundation of Christian faith, that at last the disputants agreed: they would keep peace by mutual writings if perhaps God should open the Zwinglians’ Heart.
pass_b_english: (4) Luther: the Author marvels Strimesius cited a letter hostile to the Reformed.

He adds Marburg: Luther ranked Zwinglian errors — including denying Oral eating — as deadly assaults on faith’s foundation, so the sides agreed to keep peace in writing until God opened Zwinglian hearts.
source_text: (4.) LUTHERI, cujus Testimonium miratur à me allegatum, quippe, ex Epistola, Reformatis infesta, depromptum, maximè, cùm notum prætereà sit, Lutherum Marpurgi, ubi de Cœna S. inter Lutherum & Zwinglium disceptatum potissimum fuerat, errores Zwinglianos, interque eos, Oralis Manducationis inficiationem, adeò exitiales & fundamentum christianæ fidei impetentes æstimasse, ut proptereà tandem ita inter Disputantes conventum sit: Pacem se habituros mutuis scriptis, si fortè Deus Zwinglianis Cor aperiat.
